head_commit.message:
fix: add path validation to prevent path traversal attacks in image uploads

This commit addresses a critical security vulnerability where image file paths
were accepted without validation, allowing potential path traversal attacks.

Security improvements:
- Added validateFilePath() utility to validate and sanitize file paths
- Prevents null byte injection attacks
- Blocks access to sensitive system directories (/etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, etc.)
- Resolves symbolic links to detect paths outside allowed directories
- Validates file existence and accessibility
- Ensures paths don't traverse outside allowed base directories

The fix includes comprehensive test coverage for all security scenarios including
path traversal attempts, null byte injection, symlink attacks, and sensitive
file access.

Files changed:
- sdk/typescript/src/pathValidation.ts: New validation utility
- sdk/typescript/src/thread.ts: Updated to use path validation
- sdk/typescript/tests/pathValidation.test.ts: Security tests

workflow_runs.display_title: avoid hang after child exit when descendants keep stdio open

head_commit.message:
core(exec): avoid hang after child exit when descendants keep stdio open

Some commands (e.g. test runners like Playwright) spawn grandchildren that inherit stdout/stderr. Those descendants may keep the inherited FDs open after the main child process exits. Our previous implementation waited for EOF on the pipes, so we could wait forever even though we already observed the child exit (or timeout), leaving Codex blocked.

This change ensures we don’t block indefinitely:
- Stream stdout/stderr into channels while the child is alive.
- After the child exits, drain available output for a short grace period (300ms).
- Abort the reader tasks if they’re still blocked, so we don’t rely on EOF from descendants.

Behavioral notes:
- We may miss late bytes that arrive after the grace window in pathological cases. This is an intentional trade-off to guarantee termination.
- Aggregated output still collects during runtime; the grace period just sweeps remaining buffered data.

Files:
- codex-rs/core/src/exec.rs: adjust consume_truncated_output and read_capped to use per-stream channels and timed drain, then abort readers.

Rationale:
- Fixes a class of hangs observed after commands report a non-zero exit (e.g. npm run e2e) but stdout/stderr aren’t closed due to lingering descendants.

head_commit.message:
fix: pin musl 1.2.5 for DNS fixes (#6189)

## Summary
musl 1.2.5 includes [several fixes to DNS over
TCP](https://www.openwall.com/lists/musl/2024/03/01/2), which appears to
be the root cause of #6116.

This approach is a bit janky, but according to codex:
> On the Ubuntu 24.04 runners we use, apt-cache policy musl-tools shows
only the distro build (1.2.4-2ubuntu2)"

We should build with this version and confirm.

## Testing
- [ ] TODO: test and see if this fixes Azure issues
